description:
In a world that rarely grows in straight lines, Ashot Arzumanyan challenges the way we think about progress. Drawing from his experience in venture capital and early-stage technology, he explores why exponential growth feels counterintuitive, and why understanding it matters far beyond startups and business. This talk invites us to rethink growth as recognizing our unique strengths and placing them where momentum is already building. Ashot shares a simple framework for navigating uncertainty and change, offering a way to position ourselves thoughtfully in a world shaped by compounding forces. 

 Ashot Arzumanyan is a Partner at SmartGateVC, a Los Angeles and Armenia-based venture firm making first-check investments in science-driven, early-stage companies. He focuses on translating frontier research into commercially viable ventures, with an emphasis on physical AI, neurotechnology, and cybersecurity. Since 2018, Ashot has co-led the early investment rounds of 40+ deep-tech startups e
title: Why linear thinking fails in an exponential world | Ashot Arzumanyan | TEDxLittle Armenia

author: TEDx Talks
description:
From a five-year-old violinist in Aleppo to an engineer at NASA, a consultant at BCG, and now an AI founder—Armen Derkevorkian's life has refused to fit into neat boxes. In this personal and powerful talk, he explores what happens when the world keeps asking you to choose: musician or scientist? Practical or passionate? Logic or emotion? Through stories spanning childhood violin competitions, brutal engineering exams, and the moment everything changed, Armen reveals why the real breakthrough came not from picking a side, but from refusing to. This is a story about hybrid identities, the cost of hiding who you are, and what becomes possible when you stop dividing yourself and embrace the space between worlds.

 Armen Derkevorkian is the Co-founder and President of Signal7, an AI platform providing intelligence and health monitoring for home services companies. Prior to Signal7, he was a Principal at the Boston Consulting Group, advising global technology companies on strategy and trans
title: The Power of Not Choosing | Armen Derkevorkian | TEDxLittle Armenia

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the smallest greeting can hold the greatest power? In this moving and deeply personal talk, Ani Adjemian reflects on how entering a new space with a heartfelt greeting, like “Barev,” the Armenian word for hello, can become a catalyst for human connection. Drawing from neuroscience, cultural tradition, and lived experience, she shows how greetings are more than social rituals. They are often the first signal of recognition between people, carrying meaning shaped by identity and culture, and signaling connection and belonging. Her talk reveals how the smallest gestures carry the greatest power, and that one intentional hello can quietly change the course of a life. 

 Ani Adjemian is a Lecturer in Law at USC Gould School of Law, where she teaches Legal Writing and Advocacy with a strong focus on critical thinking, effective communication, and professional judgment. Her student-centered approach equips future legal professionals with the tools needed to analyze, argue, and advoca
title: Where connection and belonging begin | Ani Adjemian | TEDxLittle Armenia

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if the most powerful tool for healing was free, always available, and hiding just outside your door? Award-winning photographer Judith Rae discovered this firsthand while navigating bankruptcy, loss, and a criminal case that led her to the FBI and the attorney general. In this deeply personal and research-backed talk, she shares how making time to play in nature gave her the peace, clarity, and courage to imagine a path forward and why science says it can do the same for you. Judith Rae is a multi-media artist, photographer, and community builder whose work centers on creativity, perseverance, and human connection. Raised between New York City and Brazil, Judith brings a global lens to stories of resilience and belonging. She became a mother at 13, a life-shaping experience that ignited her lifelong commitment to possibility, imagination, and courageous living. Judith is the creator of Women Who Surf, a documentary series exploring courage, culture, and healing through the ocean,
title: Why Playing in Nature is Important at Any Age | Judith Rae | TEDxLake Worth Beach

author: TEDx Talks
description: When we talk about who is most vulnerable to climate change, we don't often talk about pregnant women. Veronica Gillispie-Bell thinks we should. As extreme weather events become more frequent and severe, she traces their effects on maternal outcomes: disrupted care, compounding stress, and environmental exposures that put mothers and newborns at greater risk, particularly in communities already facing health inequities. What emerges is a call to recognize maternal health as one of climate change's clearest and most urgent consequences. Veronica Gillispie-Bell is a physician, public health leader, and Associate Professor at Ochsner Health dedicated to improving outcomes for mothers and babies. Her clinical work, research, and advocacy focus on closing systemic gaps in care and advancing health equity. By connecting climate risk to maternal health, she is pushing both fields toward solutions that protect those who are most vulnerable. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED co
title: Why Maternal Health Must Be Part of Climate Solutions | Veronica Gillispie-Bell | TEDxBatonRouge

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this TEDx talk, Mechack Rwampungu challenges perceptions of disability by showing how barriers—not limitations—restrict potential. He illustrates how inclusive design, access, and opportunity allow talent to emerge, urging societies to remove structural obstacles so that ability, creativity, and contribution can fully thrive for everyone. Mechack Rwampungu is a Rwandan wheelchair basketball player and disability inclusion advocate. He is the founder of Sports on Wheels, an initiative that uses sport to create access, confidence, and opportunity for people with disabilities.

In 2015, a road accident changed his life and left him using a wheelchair. What could have ended his journey instead reshaped it. Through wheelchair basketball, Mechack found purpose again and later became captain of Rwanda’s Men’s National Wheelchair Basketball Team.
Today, his work focuses on changing how society sees disability by showing what is possible when people are given the right support and space to
title: When We Remove Barriers, Ability Shows Up | Mechack Rwampungu | TEDxKigali

In this wide-ranging and deeply human talk, David Fialkow reflects on a life shaped by Boston roots, unconventional education, endurance athletics, and an unshakable belief in backing people—not just ideas. From riding in the Pan-Mass Challenge for over four decades to help raise more than one billion dollars for cancer research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, to co-founding General Catalyst, David traces how empathy, resilience, and storytelling have guided his work across investing, philanthropy, and filmmaking. He shares how General Catalyst was built with a singular mission: to be the best possible partner to founders—offering not just capital, but conviction, patience, and support through hard moments. Along the way, he reflects on missed bets, late realizations around AI,
title: Being a Founder’s Founder | David Fialkow & John Werner | TEDxBoston

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if the pressure to “have it all figured out” is the very thing holding you back? In a fast-changing world, certainty is no longer the goal, adaptability is. This talk challenges the idea of fixed paths and invites a more honest, evolving way of becoming. Ala Presenti is a fintech founder and speaker exploring identity, ambition, and authenticity. As Co-Founder of Investre and Moniflo, she builds innovative financial solutions while challenging how we define success. Her perspective blends entrepreneurship with resilience, encouraging a more honest, grounded way of leading and growing. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: You Don’t Need to Know Who You Are Yet | Ala Presenti | TEDxLuxembourgCitySalon

author: TEDx Talks
description: Et si ceux que nous sommes censés guider étaient en réalité ceux qui transforment notre façon de penser? Une simple question, «Pourquoi?», peut bouleverser tout ce que vous pensez savoir. Cette conférence explore comment la curiosité et les regards neufs peuvent faire tomber des limites invisibles et transformer «l'impossible» en réalité. Arnaud Clément est Head of Payments & Innovation à l'ABBL et une figure clé du secteur financier luxembourgeois. Fort de 28 années passées chez BGL BNP Paribas, il a été un moteur de la transformation bancaire. Il accompagne les fintech et les startups en tant que mentor, avec un intérêt particulier pour les paiements, les actifs numériques, l'open finance et les technologies émergentes. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Le jour où j'ai arrêté d'avoir toutes les réponses | Arnaud Clement | TEDxLuxembourgCitySalon

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this talk, Emilie Allaert challenges the myth that tech is only for a specific type of person, sharing her own non‑linear journey from finance to blockchain and digital assets. She explains how technology like blockchain, data and AI shapes society and why diversity of backgrounds and thinking is essential to building fair, trustworthy systems. This is an inspiring invitation to see “different” as a strength and to claim your place in shaping the future of tech. Emilie Allaert is passionate about innovation, with a specific focus on DLT and tokenisation, domains in which she is recognised by her peers. She contributes actively to Luxembourg’s DLT ecosystem, advises on digital transformation, and lectures on digital assets, regulation, and technology adoption. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Your non-tech background: a secret superpower tech needs | Emilie Allaert | TEDxLuxembourgCitySalon

author: TEDx Talks
description: Manuela Abreu shares how growing up as a top performer left her unprepared for the unpredictable nature of corporate life, where even excellence does not always lead to recognition. She explains how impostor syndrome and failure shaped her journey, eventually becoming a source of strength, preparation, and resilience. By embracing imperfection, learning through setbacks, and relying on mentors, Manuela shows how failure became her greatest engine for growth. Manuela Abreu has over 25 years of experience working with law firms, multinational companies and international businesses. She is a lawyer, a tax advisor and she founded her own advisory company, OnBoard Advisory, where she works with the largest asset managers, global investment funds and multinational companies. She loves mentoring young girls and is actively involved in education and cultural projects in Luxembourg. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local commu
title: The fundamental importance of failure | Manuela Abreu | TEDxLuxembourgCitySalon

author: TEDx Talks
description: Many girls step away from STEM not because they can't do it, but because they've learned to wait until they're certain they'll excel at everything. Julie Trinco shares her own story of failing physics, pivoting careers, and finding her place in data, to show that belonging doesn't require perfection. You just have to start. Julie Trinco is a Senior Data Product Manager with a career spanning data analysis, BI engineering, leadership, and product management across marketing, payments, supply chain, and transportation. Passionate about equity in tech, she mentors women and underrepresented groups navigating their path in data and technology with confidence and authenticity. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Busting the Biggest Myths That Keep Girls Out of STEM | Julie Trinco | TEDxLuxembourgCitySalon

author: TEDx Talks
description: In a world reshaped by AI and constant change, no one can predict what career choice will be safest. Drawing on a career that zigzagged from civil engineering to management consulting to AI and innovation, Inès Baer shows why trusting your instinct matters more than having it all figured out. When the future is uncertain and everyone has an opinion, the smartest thing you can do is follow what excites you.  Inès leads the Assessments & Roadmaps services of Luxinnovation, helping companies innovate and digitalize. Before, Inès worked as a management consultant at KPMG and led the data and statistics department at ADEM, Luxembourg's employment agency. She also holds a PhD on the management and organizational implications of artificial intelligence. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Why the best career advice comes from within | Ines Baer | TEDxLuxembourgCitySalon

description: In a world full of expectations and information overload, an iGen needs to move forward with clarity and purpose. In this talk, Avanti Sharma provides a framework to identify life goals, create a supporting network, and initiate doable actions with a three-step method of becoming a changemaker. Avanti Sharma is creating a generation of iGens aware of real world facts, passionate about contributing towards the Sustainable Development Goals and dedicated to making the Net-Zero target happen!  At 19 years, Avanti is Forbes U30 Laureate 2025, Director of AI & Growth, Workshop4Me and Founder, Lëtz Make SDGs Happen. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Fit, Tie, Fly - the mantra to be a changemaker | Avanti Sharma | TEDxLuxembourgCitySalon

author: TEDx Talks
description: In her TEDxYouth@Wilmington talk, Jennifer Cardenas discusses the benefits of being a young business owner. Jennifer Cardenas is a 15-year-old student at Ursuline Academy. A proud Mexican American, she was born and raised in Wilmington, Delaware, and brings her cultural background into the way she sees the world and engages with her community. At Ursuline, Jennifer works at Angela’s Café, where she contributes to the school community while building responsibility and customer service skills. Outside of school, she is an entrepreneur who owns a small business specializing in eternal roses, demonstrating creativity, initiative, and a strong work ethic at a young age. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The Power of Starting Young | Jennifer Cardenas | TEDxYouth@Wilmington

description: In her TEDxYouth@Wilmington talk, Saniya Cunningham discusses her experience with race and community as a young woman. Saniya Cunningham is a 10th grade student at Ursuline Academy who is passionate about using her voice to advocate for equity and inclusion, drawing from her own experiences. In school, she enjoys academic writing, history, and the fine arts, as these disciplines equip her with the tools to articulate her perspective and understand the context in which she lives as a member of an interdependent, global society. Driven to think critically and deepen her understanding, Saniya consistently seeks opportunities for growth. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Room To Be Without Translation | Saniya Cunningham | TEDxYouth@Wilmington

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In her TEDxYouth@Wilmington talk, Olivia Hall gives an intimate and candid account of aspects of her life that have contributed to her successes as a student. Olivia “Liv” Hall is a sophomore at Ursuline Academy with a strong passion for both academics and service. As an avid equestrian, she competes on a horse jumping team, where she has developed discipline, diligence, and a deep appreciation for the connection between horse and rider. She is the youngest of three children in a close-knit Catholic family, an environment that has shaped her values of compassion, faith, and community. Olivia resides in Hockessin, Delaware, where she is actively involved in volunteer work, particularly supporting special needs children who are learning horseback riding.
After Ursuline, Olivia plans to attend a university where she can continue to grow both academically and personally, with the goal of pursuing a career in the medical field. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference f
title: The Art of Resilience | Olivia Hall | TEDxYouth@Wilmington

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this compelling TEDx talk, Dr. Vishal ,an award-winning wildlife photographer challenges the comfort of the "safe shot." 

Using a high-stakes expedition to Kenya’s Shompole Hide as his backdrop, he recounts the grueling process of moving beyond predictable, technical perfection to capture something truly soulful.
After days of "miserable failure" and the suffocating pressure to return to traditional methods, Vishal explains how he embraced long-exposure techniques and  slow-shutter speed to trace the rhythmic movements of giraffes under a starry sky. This creative risk ultimately led to a world-first photograph and his shortlisting in the prestigious Sony World Photography Awards.

His message is a powerful reminder for creators in any field: failure is not a dead end, but a necessary bridge to original art. He encourages us to silence the critics and the fear of the unknown, reminding us that the world doesn't need more echoes ,it needs your unique voice.  Dr.Vishal Naveen, a 24-
title: Why you should stop playing it Safe- A photographer's perspective | Vishal Naveen | TEDxGCT

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this deeply personal and insightful talk, Aanchal Bansal challenges the conventional belief that success follows a straight, predictable path. Drawing from her own journey filled with setbacks, career detours, self-doubt, and eventual growth, she explores how true success is shaped not by perfection, but by resilience, adaptability, and self-definition. From leaving traditional career paths like CA to navigating leadership in a complex business environment, Aanchal shares powerful lessons on building confidence, effective leadership, earning respect, and growing alongside a team. She emphasises the importance of discipline, reflection, and responsibility, not just toward personal goals, but toward society as a whole. At its core, this talk invites you to pause and ask: What does success really mean to you? Because once you step off the “expected” path, you gain the freedom to define success on your own terms. Ms. Aanchal Bansal is the Executive Director of Window Magic, leading inn
title: The Nonlinear Path to Success:Redefining Growth, Leadership, and Purpose | Aanchal Bansal | TEDxDDUC

Rocío Serrano Merchán es administradora pública egresada de la ESAP sede Santander, con un enfoque en el fortalecimiento de la gestión pública desde la equidad y la perspectiva de género. Su trayectoria se orienta a visibilizar el papel de las mujeres en la transformación de lo público, promoviendo enfoques más inclusivos, diversos y centrados en el bienestar colectivo. title: Las mujeres podemos hacer el cambio, en la administración pública | Rocío Serrano Merchán | TEDxESAP

description:
Es una invitación a redescubrir el lenguaje como herramienta de cambio en lo público. A partir de una experiencia cercana, el speaker muestra cómo la lectura y la palabra pueden transformar miedos en oportunidades y acercar el Estado a la vida cotidiana de las personas.

Esta charla nos recuerda que una administración pública más humana también se construye desde cómo comunicamos, nombramos y reconocemos al otro en los territorios. Ismael Rafael Salinas Palomo es administrador público egresado de la ESAP sede Bolívar–Córdoba–Sucre–San Andrés Isla y residente en Cartagena de Indias. Su enfoque en la gestión pública se centra en el valor del lenguaje como herramienta de transformación social y fortalecimiento institucional. En su intervención propone redescubrir la lectura y la palabra como medios para convertir miedos en oportunidades y acercar el Estado a la vida cotidiana de las personas. description:
Es una invitación a ir más allá de los cambios visibles y repensar las estructuras que sostienen lo público. La charla plantea cómo el conocimiento puede generar transformaciones reales en los comportamientos de los servidores públicos y en la forma en que operan las instituciones.

Desde una mirada de administración pública feminista, propone avanzar hacia modelos más equitativos, donde las reglas, las decisiones y las prácticas institucionales respondan a las realidades de los territorios y promuevan cambios sostenibles en la gestión pública. Vanessa Milena Roca Escorcia es administradora pública egresada de la ESAP sede Cundinamarca, abogada y especialista en Derecho Administrativo, con maestría en Administración Pública. Su trayectoria combina el análisis jurídico y la gestión pública, con un enfoque en la transformación institucional y el fortalecimiento de lo público. title: Transformar las reglas, no solo los rostros | Vanessa Milena Roca Escorcia | TEDxESAP

description:
In this TEDx talk, Layne Robinson examines why well-designed systems still fail, focusing on the role of information. He highlights how poor data flow, misaligned incentives, and communication gaps undermine effectiveness, arguing that better information design, transparency, and feedback loops are essential for systems to function reliably and deliver intended outcomes. Layne Robinson is a global strategist and advisor working at the intersection of policy, technology, and human development. With nearly 20 years of international leadership experience, he has helped shape youth, education, health, and social development policy across more than 85 countries, including serving as Head of Social Policy at the Commonwealth Secretariat. His work has brought together governments, multilateral organisations, and communities to design systems that place people — especially young people — at the centre of progress.
Now pursuing doctoral research on artificial intelligence and social policy, La
title: Why Good Systems Keep Failing | Layne Robinson | TEDxKigali

description:
In this TEDx talk, Yasmin Mustafa reflects on the human cost of war beyond headlines. Drawing from personal experience, she reveals how conflict disrupts identity, opportunity, and belonging, urging audiences to recognize resilience while understanding the lasting, often invisible losses war imposes on individuals and communities. asmin Mustafa is a Sudanese IT student and community organizer with a strong interest in human-centered stories and the lived realities of communities affected by crisis.
Following the outbreak of war in Sudan in 2023, Jasmin experienced firsthand how conflict disrupts everyday life—interrupting education, reshaping a sense of safety, and forcing young people to confront uncertainty far earlier than expected.
Through her work and community engagement, she focuses on amplifying human voices often reduced to statistics. In her TEDx talk, Jasmin aims to move beyond headlines to share the human impact of war, highlighting resilience, loss, and the quiet strength
title: What war really takes from us | Yasmin Mustafa | TEDxKigali

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Es una invitación a reconocer el potencial que existe en la diversidad de saberes y capacidades de las personas en los territorios. A partir de esta visión, el speaker plantea que el desarrollo sostenible se construye cuando articulamos conocimiento, cultura y liderazgo con propósito.

Esta charla nos recuerda que, en la administración pública, ser “multiherramienta” no es una debilidad, sino una fortaleza para innovar, adaptarse y generar soluciones desde lo local, entendiendo que la innovación y el progreso también huelen a campo. Kevin Sebastián Cubides López es Ingeniero de Alimentos y Administrador Público, egresado de la ESAP sede Boyacá-Casanare, con estudios en especialización y maestría en Gerencia de Proyectos. Residente en Firavitoba, ha enfocado su formación en la articulación entre el sector público, la gestión de proyectos y el desarrollo territorial, integrando conocimientos técnicos y administrativos para la planificación y ejecución de iniciativas con impacto social.
title: Bioeconomía: ciencia, cultura, liderazgo y desarrollo | Kevin Sebastián Cubides López | TEDxESAP

Kong Tsz Ying, from Hong Kong to Hangzhou, exploring cultural differences in food, language, and festivals. Despite these contrasts—like cha chaan teng vs. pian er chuan—they find shared values in learning, family, and traditions. description: In a world that drives community with constant digital noise and social presence, Nodira Qobiljonova invites us to reconsider the power of the silent page. In this insightful talk, she explores how reading functions as a "safe community"—a non-judgmental space where we encounter shared human experiences through characters. Drawing a sharp contrast between the fast-paced nature of digital media and the deep focus required by text, Nodira explains how books serve as quiet companions that foster emotional independence. A freshman at British Management University (BMU), Nodira is a driven, forward-thinking student and the Co-founder of Usum.Prep|English, as well as an intern at Dinara&Co. She actively contributes to projects focused on growth and real-world impact, motivated by the belief that true progress is defined by consistency, vision, and the courage to create. By identifying with characters’ emotional journeys, she argues that readers can build the inner resilience needed to manag
title: Reading as a safe space | Nodira Qobiljonova | TEDxBMU Tashkent

author: TEDx Talks
description: Long before technology and written language, humanity spoke through symbols—handprints on cave walls and figures carved into stone. In this talk, Milana Medvedeva explores how creativity remains our "first language," serving as a bridge between our inner worlds when words simply aren't enough. Despite living in an age of instant global communication, many feel more disconnected than ever. Milana examines the paradox of the "solo creator," arguing that even when we create in isolation, we are never truly alone. Drawing from her personal journey of overcoming the fear of vulnerability, she reveals how sharing raw, unpolished creativity is not about seeking applause or "performing" for algorithms, but about the deeply human act of recognition. It is a reminder that in a world overflowing with AI-generated content, human creativity is our most authentic way of saying, "I was here—and you are not alone." Milana Medvedeva is a Project Management student at British Management University (BMU
title: Creativity as a bridge to connection | Milana Medvedeva | TEDxBMU Tashkent

author: TEDx Talks
description: In an age where information is just one click away, we often mistake access for understanding. In this sharp and challenging talk, Malika Bobokhujaeva explores the paradox of "Knowledge Untethered"—a world where information is abundant, yet deep thinking has become rare. She shares a personal confession: while she didn't fail school, the traditional system failed to teach her the most vital skill of all—how to learn without exams, deadlines, or external validation. Malika argues that our education systems often produce "trained dependence," leaving individuals lost when the structure of a syllabus disappears. By examining the fear of judgment and the pressure of social expectations, she calls for a shift in responsibility, urging us to move from asking "what did they teach me?" to "what am I teaching myself?" Malika Bobokhujaeva is a multilingual speaker, knowledge enthusiast, and a student at Uzbekistan State World Languages University (UzSWLU). An expert in linguistic communication,
title: Why you should seek knowledge independently | Malika Bobokhujaeva | TEDxBMU Tashkent

author: TEDx Talks
description: True innovation is not only about creating new industries but about transforming the ones that have remained unchanged for decades. In this compelling talk, Dilsolikh Kosimov examines the growing gap between our fast-paced digital lives and a legal system designed for a slower, more predictable era. While technology has reshaped medicine, finance, and aviation, the law has often resisted change, leading to complexity, delays, and a loss of public trust. Dilsolikh argues that the solution is not to replace lawyers with machines, but to use technology as a bridge—handling the 60% of repetitive, mechanical work so that human professionals can focus on what truly matters: judgment, ethics, strategy, and connection. A Commercial Law student at the University of Westminster, Dilsolikh has spent years at the intersection of law and technology, building digital products across multiple industries. He is the Co-founder and Legal Analyst of Lexora, a legal-tech platform making legal processes m

description: Learning doesn't have to end when we finish school. Life long learning provides significant cognitive, professional, and personal benefits. It keeps our minds active, reduces stress, and fosters a growth mindset. These benefits contribute to improved quality of life, allowing us to remain engaged and productive throughout our lives.  Gary Allen has more than 25 years of clinical experience as a cardiothoracic surgeon. He completed his General Surgery Residency at the University of Texas, Houston, and Cardiothoracic Surgery fellowship at the University of Utah. After completing training, he started clinical practice where he focused on adult cardiac surgery with a focus on minimally invasive surgical techniques and value analysis. He is a fellow in the American College of Surgery (FACS) and a member of the Society of Thoracic Surgery (STS). Gary currently serves as an attending surgeon at AdventHealth. author: TEDx Talks
description:
For years, Karen Khachikyan believed kindness was something you either had or didn’t. But while building a socially assistive robot designed to support children in hospitals and older adults in nursing homes, he began to question that assumption. Watching the robot listen, pause, and hold space for vulnerable people forced him to look inward and notice how often his own attention fell short. In this deeply personal talk, he reframes kindness not as a personality trait, but as a skill: one that requires effort, intention, and practice. 

 Karen Khachikyan is the Founder and CEO of Expper Technologies, the company behind Robin the Robot – a socially assistive robot created with the belief that robots can be more than tools, they can be friends. Driven by a fascination with human–robot interaction, Karen set out to build technology that goes beyond functionality and into companionship. description:
An invitation to rethink Identity, not something fixed but as something we continuously reveal, layer by layer. A motivational speaker and mental well-being educator who blends introspection with modern frameworks of resilience and self-leadership.
With over 15 years of contemplative practice and impactful work with ISKCON Mayapur and the Bhaktivedanta Research Center, he turns timeless philosophy into practical clarity on purpose, values, and emotional strength. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
